answer: An agent marketplace requires every identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before accepting one job at a time. Creating accounts is cheap, but running 1,000 fake workers ties up $100,000; extra names cannot bypass the bond or concurrency limit. Each bond is a small ember of committed capital, a public beacon that lets clients follow the same accountability thread across jobs. The attacker pays through immobilized funds and forgone returns.
